Happy Man (happy@noworries.uk) wrote:
: a girl <pony@dpc.net> wrote:
: : i just wanted to share my opinion here.I find it really funny that you
: : are fans of a guy who looks down on technology....and your on a computer
: : no less! how silly.

: 4. If you are so against technology then why do you use the Internet?

: This question appears almost every week and seems to come only from
: people who have not read the Manifesto and understand it only
: superficially from what the media has told them about it. The short
: answer is that we are using the Internet to communicate with other
: revolutionaries and to spread the message of FC to others who are
: disenfranchised with the strangle hold of the system. We agree that
: technology is powerful, especially methods of communication, and we
: are using these powerful technologies solely as weapons to weaken and
: ultimately destroy the system.

: As FC wrote in the Manifesto:

: 202. It would be hopeless for revolutionaries to try to attack the
:      system without using SOME modern technology. If nothing else they
:      must use the communications media to spread their message. But
:      they should use modern technology for ONE purpose: to attack the
:      technological system.

As well, nobody out there seems to have a clue what "the technological
system" meant. 

If Kaczynski was against ALL technology, he'd probably have gone off and
joined a Mennonite community. The idea is not a struggle against
"technology" per se, but against the cult of technologism and its desire
to implement complete control over people, to make their behaviour more
predictable and conforming with the technologist's standards. 

It is sad that people constantly misunderstand this. I don't think
Kaczynski ever wrote anywhere that portable radios, for example, are evil
in and of themselves; or ballpoint pens, or casiotone keyboards, or
whatever other banal examples of technology you might think of. The
problem's not "technology" itself, but those instances in which technology
is USED with an end in mind of controlling, brainwashing, or unnaturally
altering people and the environment in order to serve the ends of the
technologists and the people who make money off them.

Writers like William Barrett and Gabriel Marcel avoided this problem of
confusion, simply by referring to the enemy as "technique" -- so nobody
understood them, but at least nobody MISunderstood them.

Gabriel Marcel is interesting in that one of his ideas was that Mass Man
(i.e., the unthinking mass) is not only built and molded by technique, but
that the cult of technology also makes him forever unable to achieve a
high enough level of consciousness to ever GRASP any argument AGAINST
technology. Thus any argument, like Kaczynski's, will only ever seem to
fall on deaf ears (although there'll be a few "individuals" who will
actually be able to understand his concepts).

Nice to see someone besides me and Shadow is posting here.
